Maria Chen: running into flakey cert verification from our Dedicated control plane when testing through the customer's proxy/VPC. only shows up under high concurrent async load. works if I retry. using a custom CA PEM passed to the client. :thinking:

Ben Patel: is this the sync or async client? can you drop the minimal code?

Maria Chen: async. simplified snippet below (sanitized):

Maria Chen: ```py
from redwood import AsyncClient
import ssl

ssl_ctx = ssl.create_default_context()
ssl_ctx.load_verify_locations('/etc/ssl/customer_chain.pem')

client = AsyncClient(api_key='xxxxx', base_url='https://private-control.example', proxies={'https': 'http://proxy.corp:3128'}, verify=ssl_ctx)

async def do_chat():
    return await client.chat.create(messages=[{'role':'user','content':'hello'}])
```

Maria Chen: error log excerpt: TLSHandshakeError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:YYY)

Sanjay Rao: does the SDK use httpx for async? if so, verify should be honored. which httpx version and python?

Maria Chen: httpx 0.23.3, python 3.11.3. behavior is weird: at low QPS it's fine. at 100s concurrent coros we see ~1-3% fails targeting two hosts in the same region.

Ben Patel: sounds like a race between connection pool creation and SSLContext construction. are you creating one AsyncClient and sharing it, or creating a client per coroutine?

Maria Chen: creating a client per coroutine during my initial load harness. when I switched to a single shared AsyncClient the failures dropped to near zero. also passing an explicit ssl.SSLContext as verify eliminated the failures in quick smoke tests.

Sanjay Rao: that strongly indicates the SDK path that wraps httpx might be building SSLContext lazily or ignoring the verify arg when proxies are active. proxies + TLS interception often lead to different cert chains per egress node; if the client builds contexts inconsistently you get intermittent failures.

Ben Patel: immediate mitigation: share one AsyncClient instance across coroutines, or construct and pass a loaded ssl.SSLContext. longer-term: SDK should expose a clear typed field (ca_bundle or tls_config) so users can pass PEM path or SSLContext and we consistently create one context at init.

Maria Chen: agreed. also fyi I reproduced by spinning up a tiny proxy that returns different leaf intermediates on different backend nodes — certs change by node and if your PEM only has the leaf intermediate for some nodes you fail intermittently. bundling the full chain fixes it.

Ben Patel: created ticket DEVEX-1493 to investigate pooling+verify race and DEVEX-1494 to track adding a typed tls config param + env var precedence for CA bundles. I'll also add a dedicated quickstart note about custom CA + proxy config (docs PR).

Sanjay Rao: request: add typing in our stubs so IDE shows `ca_bundle: str | Path | ssl.SSLContext` on both Client and AsyncClient constructors. we should also document precedence: explicit arg > REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE env > system trust.

Maria Chen: would be great to have an example in quickstart showing both methods (path vs SSLContext) and the pooling recommendation. I wasted time creating one client per task. :grimacing:

devex-bot: ticket DEVEX-1493 created and assigned to @ben.patel.

ops-bot: infra note — customer uses HA proxy cluster with TLS interception; saw related logs around 2024-10-05T14:22:00Z. forwarding to network team.

Ben Patel: action items:
- reproduce locally with a proxy simulator and confirm race (DEVEX-1493)
- implement ca_bundle/tls_config arg + typing in py-sdk (DEVEX-1494)
- add quickstart docs for Dedicated onboarding (Ben + Docs team)
- add an integration test covering per-coro client creation to prevent regressions (QA)

Maria Chen: thanks team — sharing the workaround here: either share one AsyncClient instance or pass an ssl.SSLContext loaded with the full CA chain as `verify`. also include intermediate certs in the PEM when proxies do interception. :+1:
